newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson cuts division to 3 in restructure.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson cuts division to 3 in restructure.

text.p: Telefon AB LM Ericsson said it will reduce the number of its divisions from five to three -- telephones and terminals, mobile systems, and information communications systems -- in a restructuring effective January 1, 1997.

As well as reducing its business divisions to three from five, Ericsson said in a statement it will adopt a number of measures to strengthen its marketing so as to give more comprehensive support to customers.

"Over and above our world-leading position in mobile systems and telephones we are now creating and assembling the necessary resources to become a leading supplier of systems for infokom, i.e. network solutions, and products for multimedia communications," Ericsson's managing director Lars Ramqvist said in the statement.
He noted that for the 20th successive business quarter, Ericsson had reported a positive development in orders, sales and profits.
"Our successes can be attributed to our very strong marketing organisation in 130 countries and our technological leadership," Ramqvist said.
Ericsson will continue to build on these two strengths in the future.

"But at the same time the continually changing market situation, new demands by customers and new skills, require that we develop our organisation so as to maintain and strengthen our leading position," Ramqvist added.
